32 EXPLICITLY NUMBERED CHECKLIST ITEMS (static assessment, not reviewer-executed verification):

01 — Closed ingress/correctness. src/acp.rs:2011-2023 dispatches the known Grok extension into the existing form/responder path; unknown methods receive method-not-found. src/acp/grok.rs:8-135 is a concrete decoder, not a generic provider or prose/MCP inference layer. No issue established.

02 — Exact scope. src/acp/grok.rs:18-25 validates bounded tool identity; src/acp.rs:2113-2178 requires exact current session and validates the official form scope before canonical publication. No wrong-session answer path established.

03 — Nullable optional semantics. src/acp/grok.rs:55-68 treats absent/null multiselect as single choice and rejects conflicting aliases/nonboolean values. This matches the reviewed pinned-live contract rather than coercing arbitrary input. No issue established.

04 — Schema cardinality and duplicate keys. src/acp/grok.rs:25-132 bounds question count to32, resulting fields to64 and total choices to256; duplicate question text and option labels are rejected. Optional upstream question/option IDs are syntax-validated but are not canonical identifiers; wire answers are keyed by unique question text. No cross-object response exploit established from optional ID reuse.

05 — Typed offered-value validation. src/acp.rs:871-900,2425-2551 validates required fields, types, bounds, offered choices, distinct multiselect and64KiB answer budget before Grok encoding or commit. Unknown fields/values do not become accepted answers. No issue established.

06 — Other/notes/preview fidelity. src/acp/grok.rs:137-198 requires nonempty notes for Other before commit and encodes exact selected choices, notes and applicable selected preview on the original RPC response. Values are JSON data, not shell or terminal instructions. No issue established.

07 — Unsupported action retention. src/acp.rs:893-900 rejects Grok decline before canonical work/call/selection publication. src/tui/agent.rs:1378-1384 consumes native F6 without sending a response. Unsupported decline retains the pending question rather than fabricating plan chat/skip/cancel semantics. No issue established.

08 — Exact target identity. src/acp.rs:1169-1174,2633-2657 compares target/instance/connection/session with the live instance, including explicit null bootstrap session. No stale-target rebinding path established.

09 — Authority/revocation ordering. src/daemon.rs:441-460 authorizes the target capability and invokes Authority::admit_acp; src/control.rs:1194-1216,1236-1250 rechecks current owner/reference/generation under the target lock before canonical commit. Commit and revoke share that ordering point. No CWE-863/CWE-367 bypass established.

10 — Captured draft authority. src/tui/agent.rs:194-243,1285-1305 retains captured tuple/control/generation and discards changed authority. src/tui/control.rs:363-379 dispatches the captured action without substituting a later token. No stale draft replay path established.

11 — Original attachment provenance. src/tui/control.rs:147-241 uses the original persistent attachment worker for typed actions and view facts. src/control.rs:1207-1209 records native activity only for the original native connection. Borrowed capability use does not manufacture original-human provenance. No issue established.

12 — First-valid response admission. src/acp.rs:1971-1991 requires the exact pending canonical interaction/revision/responder. src/acp.rs:944-979 reserves capacity before publishing work and selection under the state lock. No duplicate first-valid selection path established.

13 — Responder reuse/write race. src/acp.rs:474-508,1993-2009 retains unresolved wire responder identity until actual response write completion; pointer-qualified write bookkeeping cannot retire a replacement responder. Legal completed wire-ID reuse does not revive a stale canonical interaction. No issue established.

14 — Explicit interrupt and reservation. src/acp.rs:826-862,934-978 requires the exact foreground prompt and reserves session/cancel plus mandatory original-response frames before selection publication. src/acp.rs:152-180 preserves protocol-specific cancel responses. No partial-admission cancellation defect established.

15 — Late cancel-time requests. src/acp.rs:2050-2090 commits applicable late forms/permissions as selected-cancelled before publication, including Grok outcome:cancelled. No temporary selectable window established. Original prompt completion remains the interruption outcome boundary.

16 — Force, caller loss and accepted work. src/acp.rs:1556-1611 consumes accepted immutable frames without a later-owner lookup. No force-to-process-kill/session-cancel coupling is introduced by this integration. Reviewed backend/native acceptance source checks retained original work through authority transfer. No accepted-call discard/replay defect established.

17 — Lock order and concurrency. src/control.rs:148-160,1194-1216; src/daemon.rs:255-289; src/acp.rs:1698-1758 preserve target->broker/state ordering and release topology before ACP projection. No reviewed state->authority cycle or blocking pipe/process wait under authority/state locks was established. No concrete CWE-833 finding.

18 — Frame admission. src/acp.rs:1615-1695 caps production accumulation before extension/deserialization. Oversized, incomplete or malformed transport fails the exact instance rather than silently dropping data and claiming continuity. No operational frame-bound defect established.

19 — Queue/schema/resource accounting. src/acp.rs:352-394,444-472,1646-1684 accounts for reader-owned reserved accumulation and queued/in-flight writer frames, with bounded interaction retention and outbound RPCs. No concrete operational resource must-fix established. Speculative CPU/memory/DOS concerns are not promoted to supported vulnerabilities under the skill exclusions.

20 — Closure and outcome truth. src/acp.rs:396-442; src/control.rs:1210-1215; src/daemon.rs:461-464,494-502 end authority before outside-lock cleanup and mark unresolved work unknown, not confirmed interruption. A protocol permission reject_once may legitimately finish the original prompt as cancelled without session/cancel; that is not a force cancellation. No issue established.

21 — Process ownership and launch boundary. src/acp.rs:1223-1232,1350-1420 and src/runtime.rs:716-818 use direct absolute argv spawn, setsid, birth-qualified process capture/termination and truthful uncaptured-descendant uncertainty. Operator-selected executable configuration is privileged local configuration, not a remotely untrusted shell command. Agent-owned tools are not sandboxed by amux. No supported CWE-78/CWE-269 exploit established.

22 — Pipe lifetime and joins. src/acp.rs:1237-1348,1481-1513 retains original endpoint Files through idle/early-worker exit, supports sticky independent wake, joins workers and probes endpoints before dropping descriptors and publishing cleanup. The new codec does not remove the inspected retained-pipe lifetime fixes. No concrete operational cleanup must-fix established.

23 — Cleanup certainty and charged capacity. src/acp.rs:307-311,1481-1513 keeps process-identity/endpoint uncertainty failed and capacity-charged. Unknown escaped holders are not signalled merely to obtain a successful cleanup claim. No false release of capacity established on the reviewed paths.

24 — Native deliberate action UX. src/tui/agent.rs:1315-1390,1652-1726 uses press-only response keys, two-step validation/review, observer rejection and canonical rather than optimistic accepted history. Native Grok accept/cancel availability is explicit. No security/operational must-fix established.

25 — Raw input exclusion and replay. src/tui.rs:1031-1072 consumes every active-ACP event, including None. src/tui/control.rs:363-379 retains captured envelopes without PTY fallback or automatic replay on local queue rejection. No raw-input bypass established.

26 — Terminal rendering. src/tui/agent.rs:1800-1915,2227-2269 and src/acp.rs:2690-2728 render schema/tool/preview/selection content through bounded inert display text. ESC/control/bidi marks do not reach a terminal-command sink through this path. No supported CWE-116 terminal-injection finding established.

27 — Privacy and local content access. src/acp.rs:1012-1072,1181-1207,1930-1954 distinguishes metadata-only inspection/events from explicit conversation content reads. src/client.rs:117-134 and src/daemon.rs:1965-1985 enforce the private runtime/socket boundary. Provider errors retain categories/codes rather than raw content; stderr is retained privately/bounded rather than projected into global metadata. No credential exposure established.

28 — Offered permissions/capabilities. src/acp.rs:908-931,2019-2023,2179-2227 requires an exact offered opaque permission ID and known disposition kind, never fabricates allow_once and rejects unsupported client services. No URL opening, filesystem/terminal delegation or credential-form workflow was added. No supported CWE-862 bypass established.

29 — Transparent live observer and spend evidence. tests/fixtures/acp_live_observer.mjs:16-43,68-91,135-170 uses private0600 inputs, an exclusive budget lock, atomic count-before-forward and model/effort checks before prompts, forwarding accepted bytes unchanged with backpressure. Cumulative limits include local commands and diagnostics. This does not attest hardUSD or exact charged-provider-subrequest counts; the evidence explicitly avoids those claims. No concrete operational must-fix established.

30 — Live effect confinement and cleanup evidence. tests/acp.rs:19-23,47-99; tests/acp/native/live.rs:83-205,895-1096,1212-1258 require explicit opt-in, private cwd/evidence, exact controlled effect encodings, actual allowed bytes/denied absence, restored termios, controlling-host/drainer exit, canonical close, adapter absence, daemon/socket/root cleanup and unrelated sentinel survival before fallback. The shell command is test-only and confined to approved private paths, not added to production. These checks do not sandbox an adapter. Private OAuth-root holder/removal proof remains attributed parent evidence, not reviewer observation. No supported vulnerability or concrete operational must-fix established.

31 — Test quality and causal assertions. src/acp.rs:3364-3604 covers five Grok regressions: nullable semantics, exact original response/first winner, malformed scope/duplicates, pending+late cancellation and Other/unsupported-decline retention. tests/acp/acceptance.rs:381-947 and tests/acp/native/acceptance.rs:126-563 assert actual-child/PTY effects, stale-input rejection and cleanup before fallback rather than source-text wiring or fixture-only provider acceptance. Reviewer executed none of these tests. No test-quality must-fix established.

32 — Maintainability, conventions and limitations. The concrete private codec reuses the canonical validator/responder/admission path and fixed budgets. Cargo.toml:15-30, README.md:65-114 and CHANGELOG.md:24-25 reflect schema pin, support and limitations; no new dependency or generic provider framework is introduced in the reviewed integration. Fowler smells: existing cohesive E2E/broker Long Method/large-module complexity is a maintainability tradeoff, not a demonstrated new defect; no actionable new Feature Envy, Data Clumps, Message Chains or Middle Man established. Native terminal-only/application settlement remains best-effort/unresolved and is not promoted by this ACP verdict.
